test_title: PYST 6: SSC CPO - English (Held On: 04 Oct, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

He ate the whole bunch of grapes __under the nose__ of all of us.
solution:
The correct answer is Option (2) i.e. **'In full view of somebody'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Under the nose"** of someone: To do something openly or in such close proximity that it's easily observable by others (किसी की पूरी दृष्टि में कुछ करना)

 
 
• **Example**: The thief managed to steal the painting right **under the nose** of the security guards.
 
 
 
• **In full view of somebody: **(किसी की पूर्ण दृष्टि में)
 
 
• **Example**: He completed the magic trick under the nose of the amazed audience.
 
 
 
• This Option 2 directly reflects the idiom's meaning related to doing something openly or in such a manner that it can easily be witnessed by others around.

Therefore, the correct answer is **'In full view of somebody'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **After much persuasion:** This implies that an action was taken as a result of considerable convincing, which doesn't directly relate to the idiom's implication of doing something openly.
 
• **Sharing equally:** This option denotes distributing something in equal parts among people, which does not align with the idiom's context of the visibility of an action.
 
• **Secretly:** The idea of doing something secretly is opposite to the idiom’s actual meaning of performing an action openly or in full view of others.
